title: MSTDP: a multi-scale temporal deep learning framework for just-in-time software defect prediction with cross-attention fusion
authors: Ziyang Liu, ChunHong Yuan, Hengjun Liu et al.
problem: Offline JIT defect prediction using multi-scale (hour/day/week) temporal commit features, developer behaviour and lifecycle-aware experts; robustness to concept drift
datasets: 9 GitHub projects: brackets, camel, fabric, jgroups, neutron, nova, npm, spring-integration, tomcat (Table 1; 9,258-61,364 commits; defect rate 29.37%-43.14%); labels via SZZ
split_protocol: Chronological 80/20 train/test split (Sects. 3.4.3 and 4.1.4); drift analysis with sliding windows (15-day window, 7-day step, train on prior history) and synthetic sudden/gradual feature-offset drift injection. No verification latency / label-delay modelling; not prequential
method: Multi-scale temporal LSTM/attention module + cross-attention semantic-temporal fusion + developer embedding/LSTM + lifecycle mixture-of-experts; BCE+L2 loss
baselines: JITBoost, FENSE, JIT-CF, TLEL, MULTI, DWA_JIT, EALGB
metrics_headline: Table 2 average: Acc 0.7689, Prec 0.6102, Rec 0.6782, F1 0.6093, AUC 0.8188 (best baseline JITBoost F1 0.6047, AUC 0.8136)
seeds_stats: Seeds not stated; Wilcoxon signed-rank vs JITBoost p=0.0312, FENSE p=0.0156, JIT-CF p=0.0078 (Sect. 4.2.3)
compute: NVIDIA 'H80' GPU (96GB) as written, Intel Xeon Gold 6248R, 128GB RAM; PyTorch 1.9.0
relevance: Closest paper (JIT-SDP, same 9 project names as a subset of Cabral et al.'s 14) but batch chronological split with SZZ labels treated as final; no waiting time, no provisional-clean re-weighting; commit counts/defect rates differ from Cabral ICSE'19 data so NOT directly comparable

title: DMAE: dual-memory active ensemble learning for multi-class imbalanced concept-drifting data streams
authors: Meng Han, Yajie Xue, Yikai Li et al.
problem: Online classification of multiclass imbalanced, concept-drifting streams under a limited labelling budget (active learning)
datasets: 15 synthetic MOA streams (RandomRBF/RandomTree; streams 12-13 include label noise) + 5 KEEL real streams: diabetes, penbased, banana, letter, ring (Table 2)
split_protocol: Interleaved test-then-train (prequential) in MOA; global labelling budget 20%; block size 500; 500 initial instances
method: Ensemble + drift detector + instance/label sliding windows + long-term prototype memory; BAM2-Lite variable-threshold uncertainty querying; SDMI dual-memory init; PDSR soft replacement; PCN-Weight sample weighting (boundary difficulty, imbalance, prototype relation, temporal decay)
baselines: ROSE, CALMID, AdaOB, OALM-MI, KUE, MicFoal, CSMOTE, SRP, MOOB, CSARF (Hoeffding Tree base learner)
metrics_headline: Table 7 meta-rank DMAE 1.06 (next CALMID 3.71); Table 5 G-Mean real streams e.g. penbased 92.20, letter 70.94, diabetes 44.08 (ROSE 45.3 best on diabetes)
seeds_stats: 'multiple independent random seeds' (number not stated); Iman-Davenport test + Nemenyi post-hoc (CD 2.655) (Tables 10-11, Figs 9-12)
compute: Windows 11, AMD R7-7840H CPU 3.80GHz, 32GB RAM; MOA
code: 'available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request' (declarations); Data availability section says no datasets generated
relevance: Online imbalanced drifting streams with sample re-weighting and partial labels (active budget), but labels are either queried immediately or never; no verification latency or provisional-negative correction

title: ADAWU-IDS: a dynamic adaptive weight update mechanism for concept drift-aware network intrusion detection systems
authors: Jinliang Yuan, Yu Yang, Mingqi Wang
problem: Concept-drift-aware network intrusion detection with interpretable drift-severity index and validation-calibrated response policy
split_protocol: Strictly chronological partition; chunk-wise predict-then-update (labels of a chunk used only after prediction, described as 'delayed labels'); validation-only calibration on Thursday WebAttacks stream
method: Ensemble of K LSTM learners with Multi-Scale Drift Index (MSDI) and Adaptive Drift-Aware Weight Update (ADAWU); optional hierarchical retraining chosen on validation
baselines: Static LSTM, DWM, Online Bagging, Leveraging Bagging; ablation variants
metrics_headline: Table 3 (CICIDS2017, mean±95%CI, 3 runs): ADAWU-IDS-Cal W-F1 0.9022, Attack F1 0.7831; Static LSTM W-F1 0.8865; Leveraging Bagging best W-F1 0.9859, Attack F1 0.9663
seeds_stats: 3 random seeds/repeated runs; paired t-test and Wilcoxon vs Static LSTM (Table 4): W-F1 t-test p=0.0562, Wilcoxon p=0.2500 - not significant
relevance: Online drift-aware re-weighting of ensemble members (not of training labels); labels arrive one chunk later and are assumed correct, so no verification-latency label noise

title: Statistical Drift detection with parametric Gamma-Weibull and adaptive deep learning for malware detection in IoT data streams
authors: Friday Ikechukwu Agu, Robert Andok, Jaromír Klarák et al.
problem: Drift detection (Gamma-Weibull log-likelihood CUSUM) and post-drift adaptation of LSTM/CNN malware detectors in IoT streams
datasets: Simulated IoT sensor streams with known change points; IoT-23 (benign CTU-Honeypot-Capture-4-1 + malware captures)
split_protocol: Sequential stream: model trained on pre-change segment, monitored online; post-drift adaptation uses pseudo-labels / clustering because post-change labels assumed unavailable
method: Gamma-Weibull LLR CUSUM detector + buffer-based fine-tuning with high-confidence pseudo-labels or clustering
baselines: Non-adaptive LSTM/CNN; detectors Page-Hinkley, ADWIN, KSWIN, DDM
metrics_headline: Table 4 (simulated, single run): adaptive LSTM Acc 0.991 / macro-F1 0.981 (baseline 0.987/0.977); CNN macro-F1 0.457->0.576. Table 7 (20 reps): GW-CUSUM delay abrupt 43.0±24.0, FA 1.2
seeds_stats: n=10 random seeds for adaptation; 20 Monte Carlo replications (Table 7); 30 MC reps (Table 10); one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank (largest p=5.7e-5)
compute: Standard CPU, no GPU; full cycle ~1.4 s
code: not stated (Data Availability: no datasets generated or analysed)
relevance: Handles unavailable post-drift labels via pseudo-labelling, not delayed ground-truth; drift detection focus, no defect data

title: Dynamic federated learning: coping with the challenge of label noise in real-time network data
authors: Chengtian Ouyang, Jiaxiang Wan, Donglin Zhu et al.
problem: Federated learning with time-varying label noise in dynamically growing client data
datasets: MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 (simulated streams: 20% initial data + 80% dynamic segments; symmetric label flipping)
split_protocol: Simulated streaming arrival per round; non-IID (and some IID) partitions; noise rate per noisy client sampled from [eps,1.0]
method: FedRnd: class-wise loss thresholds from historical data to split clean/noisy, augmentation of clean set, LogitClip, compactness-loss consistency score for aggregation weighting
baselines: FedAvg, FedDeCorr, GJS, FedLSR, FedNoRo, FedELC
metrics_headline: Table 2 (non-IID, delta=0.5): CIFAR-10 eps=0.2 FedRnd 72.94±0.25 vs FedLSR 71.33±0.12; CIFAR-100 eps=0.6 FedRnd 21.02±0.23
seeds_stats: 3 independent runs, mean±std / 95% CI; no significance test found
compute: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X, NVIDIA RTX 4080 SUPER, Ubuntu 24
relevance: Noisy labels arriving over time with loss-based sample weighting, but noise is synthetic symmetric flipping, not one-sided late-discovered positives

title: Heterogeneous stacking framework with adaptive Borderline-SMOTE for imbalanced binary classification: a multi-institutional validation study
authors: Yang Zhang, Yanping Zhu, Xiaohui Wang et al.
problem: Imbalanced binary classification (5-year prostate-cancer biochemical recurrence) with stacking
datasets: Development cohort N=4,127 (22.3% BCR), external cohorts n=612 and n=489, 28 features
split_protocol: Stratified split (3,515 train / 612 internal test) + nested CV with resampling inside training folds; external validation cohorts
method: PCa-Stack: adaptive Borderline-SMOTE inside folds; RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, MLP base learners; L2 logistic meta-learner on OOF predictions
baselines: 6 clinical scores (e.g. CAPRA-S) + ML baselines incl. XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, RF, voting, bagging, homogeneous stacking
metrics_headline: Table 3 internal test: AUC 0.892 (0.876-0.908), AUPRC 0.752, F1 0.736; external AUC 0.871 and 0.858 (Sect. 4.2)
seeds_stats: BCa bootstrap B=2,000 CIs; DeLong test with Holm-Bonferroni; seeds not stated
compute: 72.4 s per fold on 'reference hardware' (hardware not specified)
code: available from corresponding authors upon reasonable request
relevance: Offline imbalance handling only (no stream, no drift, no delay); relevant only as an imbalance-baseline reference

title: A stability aware meta adaptive framework for imbalance handling in machine learning and computer vision
problem: Per-dataset selection of an imbalance-handling method using a stability-aware criterion (mean - lambda*std)
datasets: 8 tabular (credit-g, ionosphere, kc2, mammography, scene, phoneme, page-blocks shown in Table 8; 8th tabular dataset not identified in extracted text) + 4 image (CIFAR-10, SVHN, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-100 with IR=10)
split_protocol: Outer 3x5 repeated stratified CV with inner 3-fold CV (tabular); 80/20 train/validation for images
method: MARS++: meta-adaptive selection among resampling/hybrid/algorithmic imbalance methods with abstention
baselines: No resampling, ROS, RUS, SMOTE, ADASYN, BorderlineSMOTE, SMOTEENN, SMOTETomek, NearMiss, Balanced RF, Easy Ensemble, Cost-sensitive RF; AutoGluon, H2O AutoML
metrics_headline: Table 10: mean PR-AUC MARS++ 0.877 (std 0.122) vs SMOTE 0.870, ADASYN 0.864; Table 8 kc2 PR-AUC 0.959±0.015
seeds_stats: random_state=42 (Table 3); Friedman + Nemenyi; pairwise Wilcoxon with Holm - no significant differences (all adjusted p>0.05)
compute: Software env in Table 3 (Python 3.10, scikit-learn, imbalanced-learn); hardware not extracted
code: not stated (Data availability: no datasets generated or analysed)
relevance: Static imbalance handling; includes kc2 (a NASA/PROMISE defect dataset) but no temporal/online setting

title: A robust intuitionistic fuzzy variance-penalized SVM for class imbalance learning
authors: Cui Fu, Shuisheng Zhou, Xiaofang Li et al.
problem: Imbalanced classification robust to noisy/unreliable samples via membership-weighted, variance-penalised hinge loss
datasets: Artificial datasets + 22 benchmark imbalanced datasets (Table 1; e.g. Liver, Haberman, Yeast*, Block*, HTRU2, MUSK2); feature-contaminated and label-flipping variants
split_protocol: 2x stratified 5-fold outer CV, 2-fold inner CV for tuning (G-Mean); contamination only in training folds
method: VRIF-VPSVM: reliability- and imbalance-aware intuitionistic fuzzy membership re-weights hinge losses before mean/variance penalty (empirical Bernstein motivation)
baselines: SVM, CS-SVM, SMOTE-SVM, Borderline-SMOTE-SVM, ADASYN-SVM, RASVM-VP, GFSVM, RIFSVM, CGFTSVM-ID, IRIFSVM
metrics_headline: Table 3 clean: G-Mean 88.22%, AUPRC 82.41%, IBA 78.81% (CGFTSVM-ID best AUPRC 85.12%); Table 4 noisy: G-Mean 88.45%, IBA 79.22%
seeds_stats: Friedman (p<0.001) + Nemenyi CD ~3.22; seeds not stated
code: not stated; synthetic data on request
relevance: Per-sample reliability re-weighting of losses under imbalance+noise (conceptually related to down-weighting unreliable negatives) but static, no time or delay

title: FIFT: Feature Importance-Guided Fairness Testing for machine learning software
authors: Hussaini Mamman, Abdullateef Oluwagbemiga Balogun, Mustapha Maidawa et al.
problem: Search-based individual fairness testing of ML classifiers
datasets: Bank Marketing, German Credit, Adult Census, COMPAS, MEPS; four classifiers
split_protocol: Not a predictive train/test study; budget 1,000,000 samples or 1 h per method; 20% validation split for permutation importance
method: Evolutionary search guided by global permutation feature importance with Importance-Guided Hybrid Mutation
metrics_headline: Abstract/Sect. 1: 20.8%-190.4% more IDIs than strongest baseline; 2.37x-3.1x higher throughput; Table 5 LR: 651,134 IDIs on average vs AFT 442,320
seeds_stats: 5 random seeds for quartile study; paired Wilcoxon signed-rank in Sect. 5.8 (feature importance-fairness link)
compute: Intel Xeon E-2224G CPU, 8GB RAM, Intel UHD P630
relevance: Software-engineering-for-ML testing; not defect prediction or streams; low relevance

title: Leveraging data drift to optimize differential privacy in federated learning via dual-mode switching
authors: Chunxiao Yin, Kai He, Zhiyang Li et al.
problem: Privacy-utility trade-off in DP federated learning under client data drift (non-IID)

method: DSDP: gradient-sensitivity + contribution evaluation, dynamic per-client privacy budget, Gaussian->Laplace noise switching
metrics_headline: Table 2 CNN non-IID: DSDP MNIST 97.57, CIFAR-10 47.39, Fashion-MNIST 75.89, SVHN 58.64 (FedAvg w/o DP 95.56/45.43/70.30/55.80)
seeds_stats: not stated; no statistical test found
compute: Intel Core i7-12700H, NVIDIA RTX 3060 Laptop GPU
code: not stated ('Data will be made available on request')
relevance: 'Data drift' here means non-IID client heterogeneity in FL; no streams, labels or delay; low relevance

title: Online label aggregation with incomplete crowd responses
authors: Yuyang Liu, Haoyu Liu, Runze Wu et al.
problem: Online truth inference from asynchronous, incomplete crowdsourced label streams
split_protocol: Online: responses arrive in chunks (size 1-100) in randomised order; use-and-discard; final and instantaneous accuracy
method: OLA-Incomplete: variational ELBO aggregator + generative replay of cumulative responses and side information
metrics_headline: Table 4 final accuracy: Duck 90.74 (chunk 40/100), RTE 92.50 (chunk 100), PostSent 95.99 (chunk 20); >=7.79% relative over strongest baseline (abstract)
relevance: Online learning where labels arrive incrementally/asynchronously and estimates are revised as evidence accumulates; analogous in spirit to provisional labels but a crowdsourcing truth-inference task
